channel.title: Multi-cluster Management on KubeSphere
channel.description: Recent content in Multi-cluster Management on KubeSphere

item.title: View Cluster List
item.description: This section describes how to view the cluster list. Prerequisites You need to have the Cluster Viewing permission on the KubeSphere platform. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with Cluster Viewing permissions. Click Cluster Management. The cluster list provides the following information: Parameter Description Name, Alias, and Description

item.title: Edit Cluster Information
item.description: This section introduces how to edit cluster information. You can edit a cluster’s alias, provider, description, and labels. KubeSphere does not support editing the name of an added cluster. Prerequisites You need to have theCluster Management permission on the KubeSphere platform. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with Cluster Management permissions. Click Cluster Management. To the right of the cluster you want to operate, click , and then select Edit Information from the dropdown list.

item.title: Add Cluster Labels
item.description: This section describes how to add cluster labels. You can use labels to categorize and manage clusters. Prerequisites You need to have Cluster Management permissions on the KubeSphere platform. You need to create cluster labels in advance. For more information, refer to Create a Cluster Label. Add Labels to a Single Cluster Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with Cluster Management permissions.

item.title: Edit Member Cluster Configuration
item.description: This section describes how to edit the cluster configuration of a member cluster, i.e., adjust the ks-agent configuration parameters. In addition to configuring the cluster when adding a member cluster, you can also edit the cluster configuration after the member cluster has been added. Note When the KubeSphere version of the member cluster is inconsistent with the KubeSphere version of the host cluster, you cannot edit the cluster configuration.

item.title: Update kubeconfig
item.description: This section describes how to update the kubeconfig information of a member cluster. After adding a member cluster to the KubeSphere platform, if the access information of the member cluster changes, you need to update the kubeconfig information of the member cluster. Note KubeSphere only supports editing the kubeconfig information of clusters added via direct connection, and does not support editing the kubeconfig information of clusters added via proxy connection.

item.title: Remove Member Cluster
item.description: This section describes how to remove a member cluster. Note The host cluster cannot be removed. After a member cluster is removed, KubeSphere will no longer be able to manage that cluster. The existing Kubernetes resources in the cluster will not be deleted. Warning After a cluster is removed, the existing multi-cluster configuration data in the cluster will not be automatically cleaned up.

item.title: Re-adopt Member Clusters to Another Host Cluster
item.description: This section describes how to re-adopt a removed member cluster to another host cluster. Unbinding a Cluster in Normal State If a member cluster is removed while in a normal state, no additional operations are required. The member cluster can be directly adopted by another host cluster. For detailed steps, please refer to Add a Member Cluster.
